workload.prompt_source: DMS data-manifest validation stream (identical token slice across arms)
workload.route_shape: one resident C1 session per arm, bulk prefill, greedy per-step decode

finding: After the wave-group6 split-K producer is enabled on gfx1100 (commit f33078ed6; previously compiled only for gfx1151), DMS-BF16 decode at 16K context is 38.14 ms/step versus the dense BF16 route's 45.89 ms/step - 17% FASTER than dense, mirroring the FastDMS-vs-vLLM result on CUDA. The kernel itself measured 4.35x faster than the generic grouped producer at live 8192 (0.344 -> 0.079 ms; ~1.9x off the bandwidth roofline). DMS INT8 remains 91.79 ms/step: its separate kernel family still uses the generic per-element-dequant producer; porting the wave6 treatment is the follow-up. Greedy tokens are identical to the pre-change DMS baseline (same eviction decisions, same outputs).
caveats: Single session, one prompt, one process per arm; diagnostics only - not a retained benchmark and no production performance claim.
The dense arm is the W7900 dense-BF16 route at the same workload; cross-GPU comparisons (e.g. against the XTX) require a same-host protocol measuring both.
The step-decomposition showed the step is GPU-bound; the host-side finalize (~1 ms) and small-kernel fusions remain available but are no longer the gap.
